newsitem.title: DUBAI: Work on $400 mln Dubai refinery to start June/July.
newsitem.headline: Work on $400 mln Dubai refinery to start June/July.

text.p: Dubai is expected to award construction work for a $400 million oil refinery in the Jebel Ali Free Zone in April and work is due to start in June or July, an official was on Monday quoted as saying.
Hussein Sultan, chief executive of the state-owned Emirates National Oil Company, said international and local firms have been asked to bid for construction of the 100,000 bpd refinery.

"We expect to receive tenders in April. Agreements with contractors will be signed in May and work is expected to commence in June or July." Sultan said in comments published in United Arab Emirates newspapers.

Sultan said the first phase of the project, due to be completed in the first quarter of 1998, will have a refining capacity of 60,000 bpd and produce jet fuel, diesel and naphtha, all meant for local consumption. It will cost $200 million.
He said condensate will be imported.
More products, including petrol and LPG, will be added to the range later, he said. The second phase, taking production capacity to 100,000 bpd, is expected to be completed in 2000.
OPEC member UAE is becoming a regional refining centre with the expansion of its Ruwais refinery in Abu Dhabi and privately-financed refinery plants.
